question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Once the responses were received, / the data collected / was tabulated for analysis.
solution:
The correct answer is "**no error**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In this case, **"data" **is treated as a **collective noun, **describing a collection of individual **pieces of information **which are considered as a **single unit. **
 
• In English, collective nouns are typically treated as singular, and so the verb should also be singular to maintain subject-verb agreement.
 
• In the given sentence, **"was tabulated for analysis"** matches in number (singular) with its subject **"the data collected."**
 
• Every part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• **Let's look at each segment:**
 
 
• **"Once the responses were received" **This is a time-dependent clause that correctly uses the past simple passive voice. It sets the precedent for the activities stated in the remaining parts of the sentence.
 
• **"the data collected" **This phrase is correct as well. It's a passive structure meaning the data that was collected. It rightfully serves as the subject of the next clause.
 
• **"was tabulated for analysis" **Again, this segment correctly uses the past simple passive voice to show what happened to the collected data.
